get.description:
Predicts the number of enquiries (leads) expected in a given
calendar month (roadmap module 20 - see ml/train_demand_forecast_model.py
for the model itself). A genuine forecast, not a lookup: works for any
future month, not only ones the model was trained on. No database
lookup here - the prediction is a pure function of (year, month).

Honest limitation: this is a linear trend + seasonal fit on ~40-50
monthly data points (mostly illustrative synthetic history - see
scripts/seed_dev_enquiry_monthly_history.py). Treat forecasts for the
next few months as a reasonable planning signal; treat forecasts more
than a year or two past the model's training data as illustrative, not
precise. Re-train periodically as more real months of leads data
accumulate (ml/train_demand_forecast_model.py always prefers real data
over synthetic where they overlap).

Scores how anomalous this lead looks compared to the rest of the
leads table (roadmap module 22 - see ml/train_fraud_detection_model.py
for the model itself). Unsupervised: there is no "confirmed fraud"
label anywhere in this schema, by design - see
ml/features_fraud_detection.py's docstring. Read-only; never writes
anything back to the lead.

Predicts the sentiment (positive/neutral/negative) of a followup's
free-text notes (roadmap module 19). Read-only: never writes anything
back to the followup.

Predicts this lead's probability of eventually enrolling (roadmap
module 13 - see ml/train_conversion_model.py for the model itself).
Read-only: never writes anything back to the lead.

Roadmap module 15 (Enquiry Source ROI Analyzer) - conversion
performance by lead source, computed live from the leads table (not a
trained model - see `note` in the response for exactly what this does
and doesn't measure).

Ranks candidate calling hours (9am-8pm) for this lead's assigned
telecaller by predicted probability of a positive response (roadmap
module 14 - see ml/train_followup_timing_model.py for the model
itself). Read-only: never writes anything back to the lead.

Predicts the probability that this application will NOT end in
application_stage == "Admitted" (roadmap module 16 - see
ml/train_dropout_risk_model.py for the model itself). Read-only: never
writes anything back to the application.

Predicts the probability that this fee_due_schedule row will go
unpaid (roadmap module 18 - see ml/train_fee_default_risk_model.py for
the model itself). Read-only: never writes anything back to the
schedule row or to fee_payments.

Ranks a telecaller's open leads (New/Contacted/Visited) by module
13's predicted conversion probability, best-first (roadmap module 21 -
same model as module 13, reframed as "which of my leads should I call
next"). Read-only: never writes anything back to any lead. An unknown
or currently-empty telecaller_name simply returns zero ranked leads,
not a 404 - assigned_to is free text, not a real FK to telecallers.

Ranks active telecallers by this lead's predicted conversion
probability if assigned to each one (roadmap module 17 - "matches best
telecaller to lead"). Reuses module 13's trained conversion model
rather than a separate one - see ml_telecaller_match_service.py.
Read-only: never writes anything back to the lead or reassigns it.

ApplicantUpdate.title: ApplicantUpdate
ApplicantUpdate.description:
PATCH model — every field optional. reg_number is deliberately
excluded: it's generated by a BEFORE INSERT trigger, and triggers
don't fire on UPDATE, so exposing it here would let a client silently
overwrite the generated, format-guaranteed value. created_by is also
excluded: it is set once at creation time from the authenticated
caller (app/services/applicants_service.create_applicant) and must
stay a reliable audit record, not something a later PATCH can
rewrite.

ApplicationUpdate.title: ApplicationUpdate
ApplicationUpdate.description:
PATCH model — every field optional. application_no is deliberately
excluded: generated by a BEFORE INSERT trigger (generate_application_no()),
and triggers don't fire on UPDATE, so exposing it here would let a
client silently overwrite the generated, sequence-backed value.

FraudScoreResponse.title: FraudScoreResponse
FraudScoreResponse.description:
Output of the module-22 fraud anomaly detector. anomaly_score
follows sklearn's IsolationForest.decision_function convention: lower
(more negative) = more anomalous, roughly 0 = the fitted normal/
anomalous boundary, positive = solidly normal - NOT a 0-1 probability
the way the classification modules' scores are. is_anomalous is the
same call ml/train_fraud_detection_model.py's evaluation used
(predict() == -1), not just a hand-picked threshold on anomaly_score.

UserCreate.title: UserCreate
UserCreate.description:
Body of POST /users (admin only). The admin sets a temporary
password and tells the person; they should change it after first login.
The password is never returned or logged.

UserResponse.title: UserResponse
UserResponse.description:
Read-only, deliberately slim view of public.users for pickers and
display (e.g. counseling_sessions.counselor_id). Only these five
columns are ever selected from the database (see users_service.py's
USER_COLUMNS) - email, phone and avatar_url are never fetched, so they
cannot leak through this API even by accident.

Matches the real public.users table (confirmed live on dev AND prod,
Sept 2026, via information_schema.columns): id uuid NOT NULL,
full_name text NOT NULL, role text NOT NULL (DB CHECK: admin /
counselor / staff / viewer - kept as free text here, not a Literal, so
the DB stays the single source of truth for the allowed values),
department text NULL, is_active boolean NULL (DB default true).

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Login and JWT-based authentication.

tags.name: Leads
tags.description: Prospective students captured before they apply - the top of the admissions funnel.

tags.name: Applicants
tags.description: Individuals who have started the application process, with full personal and academic profile data.

tags.name: Applications
tags.description: A specific programme application tied to an applicant, including seat allotment and review status.

tags.name: Fee Payments
tags.description: Payments recorded against an applicant's fees.

tags.name: Fee Due Schedule
tags.description: What an applicant owes, and by when - separate from Fee Payments (what has actually been paid). Feeds roadmap module 18 (Fee Default Risk).

tags.name: Enquiry Monthly History
tags.description: Monthly enquiry (lead) counts used as historical training data for demand forecasting (roadmap module 20). Seeded rows are illustrative synthetic history (source=synthetic); combined with live current-year counts derived from leads.created_at for training.

tags.name: ML - Demand Forecast
tags.description: Predicts the number of enquiries (leads) expected in a given calendar month (roadmap module 20). Read-only; combines seeded synthetic history with real monthly counts derived from leads.created_at; trained offline via ml/train_demand_forecast_model.py, not from live requests.

tags.name: ML - Fraud Detection
tags.description: Scores how anomalous a lead looks compared to the rest of the leads table (roadmap module 22). Unsupervised - no confirmed-fraud label exists anywhere in this schema by design; trained offline via ml/train_fraud_detection_model.py, not from live requests.

tags.name: ML - Fee Default Risk
tags.description: Predicts the probability that a fee_due_schedule row will go unpaid past its due date (roadmap module 18). Read-only; the model is trained offline via ml/train_fee_default_risk_model.py, not from live requests.

tags.name: ML - Lead Ranking
tags.description: Ranks a telecaller's open leads by predicted conversion probability, best-first (roadmap module 21). Reuses module 13's trained conversion model rather than a separate one.

tags.name: Scholarships
tags.description: Scholarship applications and awards tied to an applicant.

tags.name: Hostel Allotments
tags.description: Hostel room assignments tied to an applicant.

tags.name: Telecallers
tags.description: Staff who place outbound calls to leads.

tags.name: Document Types
tags.description: Configurable list of document types applicants may be asked to submit.

tags.name: Lookup Values
tags.description: Configurable dropdown values (grouped by type) used elsewhere in the app.

tags.name: Call Schedules
tags.description: Scheduled outbound calls to a lead.

tags.name: Campus Visits
tags.description: Logged campus visits made by a lead.

tags.name: Followups
tags.description: Logged follow-up calls made to a lead.

tags.name: Settings
tags.description: Key/value application configuration, grouped by category.

tags.name: Counseling Sessions
tags.description: Logged counseling sessions between a counselor and an applicant.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: Staff directory (active users) for pickers such as a counseling session's counselor, plus admin-only user creation. Email and phone are never exposed.

tags.name: ML - Call Sentiment
tags.description: Predicts the sentiment (positive/neutral/negative) of a followup's free-text notes (roadmap module 19). Read-only; the model is trained offline via ml/train_call_sentiment_model.py, not from live requests.

tags.name: ML - Conversion Prediction
tags.description: Predicts a lead's probability of eventually enrolling (roadmap module 13). Read-only; the model is trained offline via ml/train_conversion_model.py, not from live requests.

tags.name: ML - Source ROI
tags.description: Conversion performance by lead source (roadmap module 15). Computed live from the leads table on every request - not a trained model.

tags.name: ML - Follow-up Timing
tags.description: Ranks candidate calling hours for a lead's assigned telecaller by predicted response quality (roadmap module 14). Read-only; the model is trained offline via ml/train_followup_timing_model.py, not from live requests.

tags.name: ML - Dropout Risk
tags.description: Predicts the probability that an in-progress application will not end in Admitted (roadmap module 16). Read-only; the model is trained offline via ml/train_dropout_risk_model.py, not from live requests.

tags.name: ML - Telecaller Matching
